Question: Who would you rank as the 10 strongest Sith and Jedi of all time (Canon and non-Canon)?
Answer: By “strong” I am interpreting as “powerful” and not “physicallly strong”. Let’s go canon first. Note some of the ranked characters are tied. #1 - Darth Sidious #1 - Yoda #3 - Darth Vader #4 - Luke Skywalker #5 - Rey #6 - Mace Windu #6 - Count Dooku #8 - Obi-Wan Kenobi #8 - Anakin Skywalker #10 - Darth Maul Now for Legends. This is where it becomes interesting, and I think where most of the controversy will be. #1 - Luke Skywalker #2 - Darth Sidious #2 - Anakin Skywalker/Darth Vader #2 - Yoda #5 - Darth Traya #6 - (Darth) Revan #7 - Starkiller #8 - Satele Shan #9 - Exar Kun #10 - Mara Jade Honestly, there are too many characters in Legends with similar power levels, that I don’t think a ranking is possible. It’s also very hard to objectively compare power levels and it’s all just down to personal preference. You could argue that Exar Kun is stronger than Darth Traya, for example. The only sure thing is that Luke is the strongest Jedi, and Sidious is the strongest Sith. All the rest are up for grabs.

Question: What if the Droid army shut down command failed?
Answer: A little bit more hassle for the Repub- I mean, the Empire, but probably not too much trouble. The important thing is that all the Separatist leaders were dead. Dooku is gone. Grievous is gone. Even the useless yet still somewhat useful Gunray is dead. What are the Separatists left with? A disorganized bunch of fighting droids. The Separatists were already on the decline out when Dooku died, but then at least Grievous could still manage. Grievous is the last strong figure who can hold everyone together. This is why the Republic expected that after Grievous is killed, the war is as good as won. Now that all of the higher figures of authority are gone, there is nobody to hold things together. All the different commanders, especially the organic ones, will struggle against each other. Even if by some miracle they all agreed to collaborate, they will still lack coordination and logistics. They will still be a nuisance, and possibly take many years to clear up, but it wouldn’t be too significant. To make a chess analogy, it’s an end game without any counter chances for the opponent, even though it might take twenty more moves to close out the win.

Question: What happens when you attempt to pierce a mirror with a lightsaber?
Answer: The mirror gets burned and melted. I can guess where this is coming from, but unfortunately, a lightsaber is not a sword of “light” or a laser sword. So the mirror wouldn’t reflect it. A lightsaber is made of plasma, which is a type of matter. The plasma would simply burn and melt the mirror. As a bonus, even if a lightsaber was made of lasers, the mirror still gets destroyed. A mirror doesn’t actually reflect all the light. It still absorbs some of the light, so the laser would still affect it. A high-powered laser that can cut through steel like a knife through butter will have enough energy to destroy the mirror too.

Question: Will we see Darth Plagueis, childhood or younger version of Palpatine, Master Yoda, Tarre Vizsla in upcoming Star Wars The Acolyte TV series?
Answer: I don’t think we know the answer. The only thing that I can say for sure is that we won’t be seeing Palpatine. The Acolyte is said to take place about 100 years before The Phantom Menace. Palpatine was only 52 in The Phantom Menace. So, we won’t be seeing someone who has not been born yet. Though, the way things have been going recently, they might still shove him in there regardless, maybe as a Force vision or something. I surely hope not. That said, despite the possibility, I would personally much rather that none of these characters appear. Not even Plagueis, who I do want to see more of in an official animated or live action medium. Most of the best Star Wars stories recently have been independent stories featuring new characters. The Mandalorian Season 1 (and Season 2 to an extent), Rogue One and Andor, etc. There are still tie-ins and connections to other stories, but mostly as Easter eggs or bonus side characters, not as an integral part of the narrative. In contrast, some of the worst ones were ruined by contrived connections to pre-existing characters and stories. Solo probably wouldn’t have been so hated if they just did an unrelated young smuggler, instead of messing with Han’s character unnecessarily. The Mandalorian series might still be going strong and loved better than ever, if they had stuck to their guns and didn’t bring back Grogu, or force his appearance in the Book of Boba Fett. And don’t even get me started on the Kenobi show, which I’ve come to dislike, despite initial efforts to force myself to like it. I would prefer that The Acolyte series be a fresh, creative story. Come up with something interesting and new. Anything in the Star Wars universe already has so much brand recognition and appeal to a large fan base, you don’t have to awkwardly make everything connected. Tell an interesting story. Build up interesting characters.
